![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/7178cf6a642786f249a22cab09178eaa62e63e47a4e3bb28969ca90f4d97db95.png)

The scatter plot above shows the distances some athletes in a sports club cover during a training session, and the time (in minutes) it takes. Use the trend line to estimate how long it takes a club athlete to run $10$ km.
question.worked_solution:
To make our estimation, we proceed as follows:

- We start at $y=10$ on the vertical axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/c595c42406bbf7ad4d71b6ceb9914b839f529b26135c467231a38b3cc48223c8.png)

- Then, we move right until we intersect the trend line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/28f757380ba22cddc96fbd382578a6b8dc9bba258adfec704413047e73d54c93.png)

- Finally, we move down until we intersect the horizontal axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/85754fb62bbee8c597a71ad8fe30e5eabca3ed9c6304b1832e14788b1e809bcd.png)

Therefore, a club athlete can run $10$ kilometers in approximately $45$ minutes.
